title: Quarterly cycle staffing & scope trade-offs: playbook and allocation model
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: produce an operational playbook and numeric allocation model to guide quarterly cycle staffing, scope prioritization, and emergency capacity buffers. Background: recent cycles have seen repeated scope creep and mid-cycle re-prioritizations that caused missed SLAs for Dedicated capacity features and pushed back two infra optimizations. This ticket consolidates learnings, defines a repeatable staffing allocation process, and publishes a lightweight decision matrix PMs and ENG leads can use during sprint kickoff.

Deliverables:
- A one-page playbook (Confluence) describing roles, allocations, and cut rules.
- A spreadsheet model with allocation presets (Core platform, Dedicated, Private deployment, Console, Lifecycle/rollouts, Unplanned ops buffer).
- Example runbook for scope cuts and last-resort deferrals tied to OKR health.
- Communication templates for stakeholders and sales when scope changes impact committed dates.

Business constraints and assumptions:
- Total available product FTE for Q2 assumed at 14 (PM+EM combined allocation).
- Engineering capacity is constrained by GPU infra hiring lag; assume 12 effective eng FTEs for prioritization modeling.
- Must reserve a 12% buffer for incident-driven work and P0 reliability fixes.
- Feature work tied to revenue (Dedicated contracts) gets priority for release windows tied to customer SLAs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook published in Confluence with sign-off from Head of Product and two ENG leads.
- Allocation spreadsheet accepts inputs for team size and outputs recommended story point budgets per initiative with a visual "cut-line" showing where scope is trimmed.
- Two simulated run-throughs with PM+ENG leads that demonstrate scope cut decisions for at least two scenarios (hiring shortfall, unexpected infra regression).

Success metrics (how we'll know it helped):
- Fewer mid-cycle reprioritisations (target: reduce by 60% vs last two cycles).
- Less than 10% of planned stories carry over to next cycle for scoped initiatives that followed the playbook.
- PM/ENG satisfaction score for planning process >= 4/5 in post-cycle survey.

Notes on trade-offs and open decisions:
- Trade-off A: strict allocation (fixed buckets) vs flexible pool. Recommendation: hybrid model with fixed critical buckets (SLA features, infra reliability) and a flexible pool for experimental work.
- Decision needed by 2026-03-18 on whether to reclassify "Optimize batching heuristics" as SLA-tied (candidate for critical bucket) — affects early allocation.
- We need leadership alignment on what counts as "customer SLA" for Dedicated customers (sales/CS input required).

Links and artifacts:

- Allocation model (spreadsheet): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/driveid (sheet: Q2 Allocation)
